new_types.name: AI for translation and language support
new_types.covers: Rules on using AI to translate text or to support language learning (permitted, conditioned or banned). Split out of P18 and from reviewer NEW labels.

new_types.name: AI feedback or critique on one's own work
new_types.covers: Using AI to get feedback, critique or review of one's own draft, code or solution (not to produce it). From P14, P91 subgroups and NEW labels.

new_types.name: Signs and indicators of AI-written work
new_types.covers: Manual signs, comparisons and indicators instructors use to suspect AI-written work (style shifts, fabricated citations, comparison with earlier work), as distinct from detector tools (P40) and standards of proof (P69).

new_types.name: What AI can and cannot do (capabilities and limits)
new_types.covers: Statements about AI's capabilities and limits beyond wrong output (P31): low quality, shallow reasoning, changing capability, what tools are and are not good for.

new_types.name: Status of the guidance (advisory or binding, precedence)
new_types.covers: The document says whether it is guidance or binding policy, and which text prevails when guidance and formal policy conflict.

new_types.name: Accountability for AI-assisted output
new_types.covers: Users are responsible for the accuracy, quality and consequences of AI-assisted work they submit or use (split from P29, which keeps 'submitted work must be one's own').

new_types.name: Career and workplace readiness as a reason to learn AI
new_types.covers: Preparing students for an AI-shaped workplace as the rationale for teaching or allowing AI (split from P44, which keeps teaching AI use in courses).

new_types.name: Environmental cost of AI
new_types.covers: Energy, water and carbon costs of AI named as a concern (split from P53).

new_types.name: Labor, consent and credit behind AI
new_types.covers: Concerns about uncredited labor, training on work without consent, and exploitation in building AI (split from P53).

new_types.name: AI records retention and public-records duties
new_types.covers: AI prompts, outputs and logs as records subject to retention rules or public-records requests.

new_types.name: AI is widespread and here to stay
new_types.covers: Context statements that AI is inevitable, already widespread or here to stay, used to frame the policy.

new_types.name: Purpose and context of the policy document
new_types.covers: Why the document exists, what problem it addresses and its context (split from P56, which keeps values and principles).

retired.P18: Split by second pass into P91, P16, P128, P100, P129 and other existing types; reviewers found its units are rules about AI for writing, not a prose-versus-code distinction.

P18.why: Reviewers found P18 units are writing rules (editing, translation, drafting), not a prose-versus-code distinction.

P29.why: Two contents: submitted work must be one's own vs accountability for AI-assisted output.

P44.why: Teaching AI use in courses vs career-readiness rationale vs institutional AI literacy.

P53.why: Bias/general ethics vs environmental cost vs labor and consent; teaching ethics belongs to discussing AI with students.

P56.why: Values and principles vs purpose/context vs compliance, governance, provenance and scope.

P40.why: Detection tools vs manual signs of AI-written work vs evidence standards.

P69.why: Evidence standards vs signs of AI-written work vs detector reliability.

P14.why: Study aids vs feedback on one's own work vs summarizing readings.

P91.why: Editing and outlining one's own work vs AI feedback vs AI-drafted content.

P24.why: Student and user disclosure vs labeling institutional AI content vs research disclosure vs citation details.
